assessment.calibration_basis: p_engine=0.55 sets the R2 customer-denial floor (denial not explained by R7: recurring_charge_check found 0 matching groups). I moved 0.05 above the floor, staying inside p_engine±0.10, because the card carries 3 prior confirmed_fraud closed cases (CC-3778, CC-2121, CC-1736), all card_not_present_fraud on this same card via the same online channel (flags.recent_same_channel_case=true) — a case-memory signal the floor alone does not fully capture. I did not push further toward the fraud band because the case-memory scorer (cms_p=0.007, calibrated score 0.01) and the absence of any strong shared device/ring evidence (ring_profile empty, shared_origin_scan shows only non-strong profiles) are genuinely legitimacy-leaning; verdict stays uncertain since 0.60 < 0.70 and a denial can never resolve to legitimate before a confirmation.

case_context's case-memory calibration for transaction 3583227 is cms_p=0.00701 (calibrated ~0.01), far below the bank's real-time risk_score of 0.34, indicating the memory-informed model reads this specific transaction as unusually low-risk given its features.
